sample_unit: patients (225 pulmonary hypertension, 28 interstitial lung disease)

links.outcome: Segmentation error-free rate on internal versus external validation cohorts
links.effect: 82% of internal and 71% of external cases had no errors; 18% and 25% respectively had clinically insignificant errors, and one external case (0.5%) had a clinically significant error.
links.quote: On radiological review, 82% and 71% of internal and external cases respectively had no errors.

links.outcome: Clinical significance of segmentation errors found on radiologist review of model outputs
links.effect: No segmentation failures; most cases error-free or with insignificant errors; one external case (0.5%) with patulous oesophagus had a clinically significant error.
links.quote: One external case (0.5%) with patulous oesophagus had a clinically significant error.

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an nnU-Net deep learning model for CTPA lung segmentation using retrospective cohorts and expert radiological review of failure modes, but does not test a specific operational deployment practice or safeguard.
